title: Configure Supabase
description: Set up the backend: one Supabase project with the auth providers you use enabled, its Site URL set to the app's primary origin, and its URL and publishable key available as VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (local .env, plus the hosting build variables for main and for previews). Before the app has real users, isolate staging from production with a Supabase Branching staging branch or a second project (documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md § Staging backend). Your coding agent lists the exact requirements, checks the result, and tells you what only you can do. For Google sign-in, requirements are in documentation/DOC_SUPABASE_GOOGLE_OAUTH.md. If you explicitly say this app does not use Supabase, Google sign-in, anonymous sessions, or error reporting, the agent offers to delete that code. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Shipped integrations and § Configuration tasks gate (Supabase).

title: Put your app online (Cloudflare hosting)
description: Get your app live on the internet with Cloudflare (free tier is fine). Your coding agent does the setup — just ask it to "do the hosting task". What you need ready: a Cloudflare account, your Supabase keys already in .env, and (optional) a domain name you own. How it works once set up depends on your git workflow mode (see .claude/rules/git-workflow.md § Mode behavior table, rows staging and production) — by default every pull request gets its own preview link and merging the pull request ships to production. One step happens in the Cloudflare website (connecting your repo); the agent tells you what must be set there and why, waits for you, and checks the result. Agent playbook + troubleshooting: documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md (see "Agent one-shot brief"). If you explicitly say this app does not use Cloudflare, the agent offers to delete that hosting code (there is then no preview link). Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Shipped integrations and § Configuration tasks gate (Hosting).

title: Define app vision
description: Collaborate with the coding agent to fill documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md (problem, persona, app role). Replace placeholder bullets with real prose and change Vision status from DRAFT to ACTIVE when complete. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § App vision & goals gate.

title: Make the interface yours
description: Everything visible still shows the template. Your coding agent renames the app (browser tab title in index.html, top bar in src/layouts/Topbar/Topbar.tsx), walks through the home page and top bar with you (keep or change each), and removes the harness overview card (src/features/harness-overview/, src/pages/HarnessOverviewPage.tsx and its test, the /harness route in src/App.tsx, the card in src/pages/HomePage.tsx, public/harness-overview.png, plus its README.md image and documentation/DOC_INDEX.md row). Then restyle via the design token files in src/shared/theme/tokens/ and run pnpm tokens:build (documentation/DOC_THEMING.md); verify both modes with the theme icon in the profile menu. It also replaces the template icon and adds your app icons, theme color and link-preview card (title, description, image) in public/ and index.html; you supply a logo or approve a drawn one, and paste your preview link into a chat app to check the card. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Configuration tasks gate (Interface).

title: In-app feedback widget
description: A small signed-in feedback form that writes to app_feedback with the page and environment. Depends on: Signals backend task.

title: Admin signals view and switch the signal adapter on
description: An admin-only view (role claim) to triage error clusters and feedback, and turn on loop-backlog's signal adapter so open signals become ranked backlog tasks. Depends on: Signals backend, error capture and feedback widget tasks.

title: Add a db:push-staging script or fix the adapter reference
description: The signal adapter (.agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/signal-adapter.md) tells the agent to run `pnpm run db:push-staging`, which does not exist. Either add a script that applies supabase/migrations to the staging project with a pinned Supabase CLI (needs project linking, which the owner must set up), or change the adapter to say the connector or CLI applies migrations. Protected file edit: needs owner approval. Context: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § signals-backend D8.

title: Decide whether the app uses anonymous sign-ins
description: The app asks Supabase for an anonymous session on every visit and Supabase refuses (anonymous_provider_disabled, HTTP 422), twice per page load. Either enable anonymous sign-ins in the project (anonymous users get the authenticated role, so the feedback policy would admit them; review RLS first) or remove the call. Auth permission model: needs an owner decision.
